summary: Provision 'integration-playground' Jira project + Confluence space + Slack channel with CI webhook and guest-approval gate
description:
Background: Multiple platform and product teams have asked for a standardized, short-lived integration playground that bundles a Jira project, Confluence runbook space, and Slack channel. The goal is to give cross-functional teams (eng, QA, infra) a consistent place to run integration tests, onboard third-party tools, and exercise deployment hooks without creating ad-hoc spaces that are hard to track.

Request: Create a templated, self-serviceable integration-playground offering with the items below and sensible defaults for lifecycle and security. This ticket captures the provisioning and automation requirements; implementation should be reusable and parameterizable for teams to request via an internal portal/Slack bot in a follow-up story.

Impact: Low immediate risk but high operational value — reduces setup time for integration experiments, reduces noisy ephemeral channels, and centralizes auditability for guest access and CI webhooks.
requested_items: Jira project: key INTGPLAY, project template = Software Project (Kanban) with issue types: Task, Bug, Experiment. Default components: integration, infra, ci-cd.
Confluence space: 'Integration Playground - INTGPLAY' cloned from a thin template that includes: incident playbook, runbook checklist, onboarding steps, and a 'CI webhook manifest' page.
Slack channel: private channel #intg-play-<team> created automatically during provisioning, members synced from Jira project roles; naming convention enforced.
Service account: 'svc-intg-play-bot' with scoped tokens for Slack app and a GitHub webhook user (rotated monthly).
Automation: on-create hooks that wire a repo webhook to the Confluence CI webhook manifest, and add an issue automation rule to create a runbook page when a 'Release Test' issue is transitioned.

Guest approval flow: external guests require approval from two project owners via an automated request; approval should appear as a Slack message with Approve/Decline buttons that link to Jira request.
Lifecycle policy: default expiry 14 days; channel/space/project archived at expiry and owners emailed 72h before; owners can extend once per archive cycle.
Observability: create a lightweight audit log entry (Confluence page link) summarizing provisioning params and the GitHub repo receiving the webhook.
RBAC: Project role mappings: Owners (can add guests), Members, Read-only observers; Slack members mapped to Jira roles; Confluence restrictions mirroring Jira project roles.
automation_requirements: 1) Provisioning script must use existing org templates and run with a single approval in Jira. 2) Create a GitHub webhook using a scoped service account and store the webhook secret in the vault. 3) Slack channel creation via Slack provisioning bot with membership synced from Jira project role groups. 4) Add scheduled job that checks for expired projects/spaces/channels and triggers archive workflow plus notification email. 5) All actions must be idempotent and provide human-readable audit output (timestamp, actor, params).
rbac_requirements:
- Owners group: team leads + oncall engineer (default).
- Members group: users explicitly added by Owners.
- Guests: external vendor accounts require 2-owner approval via Slack interactive message.
- Service accounts must be created with least privilege and have an automated rotation policy (30 days).
- No anonymous or public group permissions on Confluence or Jira pages created by this flow.
security_requirements:
- Webhook secrets must be stored in Vault/KMS; never placed in Confluence pages.
- Service account keys rotated automatically and usage logged.
- Provisioning job must run in a restricted runner and require token with narrow scope.
- Audit events for create/archive must flow to central audit stream (link logs to observability pipeline).
acceptance_criteria: A templated Jira project INTGPLAY can be provisioned via the internal UI or automation script with parameters for team name and expiry.
Confluence space is created from template and contains runbook and CI webhook manifest page with placeholder fields filled from provisioning parameters.
Slack private channel is created with correct name and membership, and visible in Slack for all members. Approval flow for guests functions end-to-end (request -> 2 approvals -> guest added).
A GitHub webhook is successfully created against a specified repo and triggers a test payload that creates an entry on the Confluence CI webhook page (test harness).
Expiry job archives the Jira project, Confluence space, and Slack channel and sends owner notifications 72h prior.
provisioning_flow: 1) Requestor opens a short form (internal UI or slash command) with params: team_short, owner_emails, repo_url, expiry_days (default 14). 2) Controller creates the Jira project and maps Owners/Members groups. 3) Confluence space cloned from thin template and placeholder fields replaced. 4) Slack channel created and membership synced. 5) Service account and GitHub webhook created; webhook secret stored in Vault. 6) Notification sent to owners with links and a 72h pre-expiry job scheduled.
comments: Asha Patel (2026-03-10): Filing initial request — would like a reusable implementation that teams can self-service later. Prefer a small productized UI in the portal (follow-up).

Liam O'Connor (2026-03-11): Assigned. Can we confirm if existing 'svc-provisioner' SA can be reused for webhooks or if we require a dedicated svc-intg-play-bot? Security prefers dedicated SA per environment.
Priya Ramesh (Security) (2026-03-11): Security: dedicated service account recommended. Also require monthly key rotation and audit hooks. We'll add review for vault access policy.

Diego Alvarez (Infra) (2026-03-12): Noted. I can add the webhook creation/job into the automation repo. Will need the template Confluence space exported or a short doc describing required pages/variables.
implementation_notes:
- Use platform-provisioner library for idempotent resource creation.
- Parameterize template with: team_short, owner_emails, repo_url, expiry_days.
- Vault path: secret/intg-play/{{project_key}}/webhook.
- Use existing Slack provisioning bot but extend membership sync endpoint to accept Jira role groups.
- Add unit tests for webhook lifecycle and a staging dry-run.
- Coordinate final rollout with Security and Compliance for service account onboarding.
follow_up_tasks: Create internal portal UI story to call this provisioning flow (separate ticket).
Add telemetry: count of active playgrounds and avg lifetime for observability dashboard.
Run a tabletop with two teams to validate guest-approval flow next quarter.
